correctness.rationale: The proof independently derives the gap-condition iff maximality, the local-slide iff 2/3 swap, marked gap-word and r-run counts, and connectivity via anchor-preserving adjacent transpositions plus controllable anchor displacement. The floor Beatty-type n-step process supplies the shortest odd cycle, with mod-n sum proving optimality. Wraparound and t=0 are separately handled. Two standalone verifiers enumerate independent-and-dominating configurations directly versus gap generation, reproducing counts and explicit legal n-step cycles across finite test ranges.

evidence: Bonsma et al. (2014) prove polynomial-time reachability for unconstrained independent sets on claw-free graphs; connectivity in an ambient graph does not imply connectivity of the subgraph induced by dominating sets.
Avis–Hoang (2022) treats the ambient independent-set TS graph, with no maximality predicate.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader reachability algorithm may find paths that temporarily cease to dominate, so it does not dominate the stricter connectivity claim. An ambient graph's even degrees, bipartiteness or odd-girth cannot determine an induced subgraph's degree distribution or odd girth.

originality.rationale: Compared full statements and proof scopes of Bonsma–Kamiński–Wrochna (2014), Brewster–Mynhardt–Teshima (2023), and Avis–Hoang (2022). The prior exact cycle i-graph result fixes the minimum independent-domination size, expressly excluded here; general independent-set token-sliding allows non-dominating intermediates. The all-nonminimum maximality-preserving degree spectrum and exact odd-girth conclusion are not implied by the inspected results. Relevant published-finding corpus and own archived claims did not indicate stronger coverage; a residual unindexed-publication possibility remains.
residual_risks: The complete bibliography of possible earlier maximal-independent reconfiguration papers, including unindexed or differently named structural enumerations, is not exhaustively available.
Similarity search alone cannot certify priority; claims are restricted to the exact nonminimum configuration family and move model.
